ear.transcript: After auditioning, I'm listening to D9 and I like the way it sounds a lot. The melody lines sound like they belong with the chord progressions and it catches the ear. It leaves you wanting to hear more. For D8b, the last chord sounds like it belongs the most. And the melody line sounds like it belongs, but it's pretty repetitive and there's a lot of ambiguity. I'm unsure if this is because of the node types that the progression in melody lines are using or if it's for another reason. The chord progressions for D8 sound better. Even though the melody line sounds like it's the same from D8b, the melody line and the chord progressions go together better. It still wouldn't surprise me if there was something odd about the notes that are used for this because the progressions themselves don't sound too harmonious, but they sound like they belong at least. The seventh's chord progression and melody line sound okay. The last progression sounds like maybe there's something off about it. The six sounds strong. The chord progressions and the melody cohesion sounds great, and there's a bit of variation in the melody that makes it stand out. For D5, the melody sounds like it almost matches, but the progressions themselves sound like they work. Maybe it's just not a very melodic or harmonic set of notes that are being used for this progression, but overall they sound like they work, just maybe an off note on the melody. D4 sounds great all around. The chord progressions sound like they belong with the melody line. There's variation in the melody that works, and it sounds like a very nice melody and chord progression. D3 also sounds very good. The chord progressions and melody line sound great together. D2 also sounds very good. The melody line and the chord progressions sound like they get along well. The wind sounds great as well. The chord progressions and the melody work well together, and the melody line has a variation and change to sound interesting. [STT note: 'The seventh's' = D7; 'The six' = D6; 'The wind' = D1.] Verdict: I adopt the cadence stride algebra, voice-led stack rotations (D8 [0,2,1,2] displacement 9 over D8b m=0 displacement 47, D9 r1->r0->r0), and the six-sibling family (ADOPT_CADENCE_ALGEBRA).
